title: El cuerpo y la salud
goal: Name parts of the body, say what hurts, see a doctor and say what you have to do.

lessons.title: The body
lessons.notes:
Body words, each with its article. As you saw with **me lavo las manos**, Spanish uses **el / la** with body parts where English says "my": **Levanta el brazo.** = Raise your arm.
Two words for the ear: **la oreja** is the outside part, **el oído** is the inside (and hearing).
Watch the gender traps: **la mano** (f) and **el pie** (m), **la espalda** (back, f).
Plural of **el pie** is **los pies**; of **la nariz**, **las narices** (z -> c before -es, like lápiz -> lápices).

sentences.es: Mi hermano tiene los ojos azules.
sentences.en: My brother has blue eyes.

sentences.es: Carlos tiene los brazos muy largos.
sentences.en: Carlos has very long arms.

sentences.es: El niño tiene una pierna en el sofá.
sentences.en: The boy has one leg on the sofa.
accept_en: The child has a leg on the sofa.
The boy has a leg on the couch.

sentences.es: Me lavo la cabeza por la noche.
sentences.en: I wash my hair at night.
accept_en: I wash my head at night.
I wash my hair in the evening.

sentences.es: Tengo los pies muy fríos.
sentences.en: My feet are very cold.

sentences.es: El gato duerme en mi espalda.
sentences.en: The cat sleeps on my back.

sentences.es: El bebé abre la boca para comer.
sentences.en: The baby opens his mouth to eat.
accept_en: The baby opens her mouth to eat.
The baby opens its mouth to eat.

sentences.es: Mi bebé tiene la nariz de su papá.
sentences.en: My baby has his dad's nose.
accept_en: My baby has her dad's nose.
My baby has its father's nose.

sentences.es: El cuerpo necesita agua.
sentences.en: The body needs water.

lessons.title: It hurts
lessons.notes:
**doler** (to hurt) works exactly like **gustar**: the part that hurts is the subject, the person is **me / te / le / nos / les**.
**Me duele la cabeza.** = My head hurts / I have a headache.
**Me duelen los pies.** = My feet hurt (plural -> **duelen**).
**¿Qué te duele?** = What hurts? / Where does it hurt?
It's o -> ue: **duele**. Past: **me dolía** (it was hurting) or **me dolió** (it hurt, once).
Other ways to say you're unwell use **tener** or **estar**: **tengo fiebre** (I have a temperature), **tengo tos** (a cough), **estoy enfermo** (I'm sick), **estoy resfriado** (I have a cold).

items.note: Works like gustar: me duele, me duelen.

sentences.es: Me duele mucho la cabeza.
sentences.en: I have a bad headache.

sentences.es: ¿Qué te duele?
sentences.en: What hurts?

sentences.es: Me duelen las piernas después de correr.
sentences.en: My legs hurt after running.
accept_en: My legs hurt after I run.

sentences.es: A mi hijo le duele el estómago.
sentences.en: My son has a stomach ache.
accept_en: My son has a tummy ache.

sentences.es: Ayer me dolía la garganta.
sentences.en: Yesterday my throat was sore.
accept_en: Yesterday I had a sore throat.

sentences.es: Estoy enfermo, tengo fiebre.
sentences.en: I'm sick, I have a temperature.
accept_en: I'm ill, I have a fever.
I'm sick, I've got a temperature.

sentences.es: Mi hija tiene tos y un resfriado.
sentences.en: My daughter has a cough and a cold.
accept_en: My daughter's got a cough and a cold.

sentences.es: Toda la familia tuvo gripe.
sentences.en: The whole family had the flu.
accept_en: All the family had the flu.

sentences.es: Hoy me siento mejor, gracias.
sentences.en: I feel better today, thanks.
accept_en: Today I feel better, thank you.

sentences.es: A Ana le duele el oído.
sentences.en: Ana has an earache.

lessons.title: At the doctor's
lessons.notes:
At the doctor's you'll hear and use:
**la cita** (the appointment) · **la receta** (the prescription - it also means recipe!) · **la pastilla** (the tablet) · **el medicamento** (the medicine) · **la farmacia**
**tomar** is the verb for medicine: **tomar una pastilla**.
**descansar** = to rest.
**¿Desde cuándo?** = Since when? / How long? Answer with **desde** + a time: **desde el lunes**, **desde ayer**.
A doctor usually speaks to you as **usted**: **¿Cómo se siente?** (How do you feel?) **¿Qué le duele?** (What hurts?)

sentences.es: Tengo una cita con el médico a las tres.
sentences.en: I have a doctor's appointment at three.
accept_en: I have an appointment with the doctor at three.
I've got a doctor's appointment at three.

sentences.es: ¿Cómo se siente hoy, señora?
sentences.en: How do you feel today, madam?
accept_en: How are you feeling today, madam?

sentences.es: ¿Desde cuándo tiene fiebre?
sentences.en: How long have you had a temperature?
accept_en: Since when have you had a fever?
How long have you had a fever?

sentences.es: Tengo tos desde el lunes.
sentences.en: I've had a cough since Monday.
accept_en: I have had a cough since Monday.

sentences.es: El médico me escribió una receta.
sentences.en: The doctor wrote me a prescription.

sentences.es: Voy a la farmacia por el medicamento.
sentences.en: I'm going to the chemist for the medicine.
accept_en: I'm going to the pharmacy for the medicine.
I'm going to the chemist to get the medicine.

sentences.es: Tomo una pastilla cada ocho horas.
sentences.en: I take one tablet every eight hours.
accept_en: I take a tablet every eight hours.
I take one pill every eight hours.

sentences.es: Necesita descansar dos o tres días.
sentences.en: You need to rest for two or three days.
accept_en: You need to rest two or three days.
He needs to rest for two or three days.
She needs to rest for two or three days.

sentences.es: ¿Tiene un medicamento para la tos?
sentences.en: Do you have a medicine for a cough?
accept_en: Do you have any cough medicine?
Have you got something for a cough?

lessons.title: I have to rest
lessons.notes:
**tener que** + infinitive = to have to, must. Conjugate **tener**, keep the next verb whole:
**Tengo que descansar.** = I have to rest.
**¿Tienes que trabajar mañana?** = Do you have to work tomorrow?
**hay que** + infinitive is the general "you have to / one must", with no person: **Hay que beber mucha agua.** = You need to drink lots of water.
In the past, use the imperfect for an ongoing obligation and the preterite when you actually did it: **Tenía que estudiar** (I was supposed to study) / **Tuve que ir al médico** (I had to go - and I went).
A kind wish: **¡Que te mejores!** = Get well soon!

sentences.es: Tengo que descansar mucho.
sentences.en: I have to rest a lot.
accept_en: I need to rest a lot.

sentences.es: ¿Tienes que trabajar mañana?
sentences.en: Do you have to work tomorrow?

sentences.es: Hay que beber mucha agua.
sentences.en: You have to drink lots of water.
accept_en: You need to drink a lot of water.
One must drink plenty of water.

sentences.es: Ayer tuve que ir al médico.
sentences.en: Yesterday I had to go to the doctor.
accept_en: I had to go to the doctor yesterday.
Yesterday I had to see the doctor.

sentences.es: Estás enfermo. ¡Que te mejores!
sentences.en: You're sick. Get well soon!
accept_en: You're sick. I hope you get better!

sentences.es: Para tener buena salud, hay que dormir bien.
sentences.en: To be healthy, you have to sleep well.
accept_en: To have good health, you need to sleep well.

sentences.es: Mi abuela tiene ochenta años y está muy sana.
sentences.en: My grandmother is eighty and very healthy.
accept_en: My grandma is eighty and she's very healthy.

sentences.es: Hago ejercicio tres veces a la semana.
sentences.en: I exercise three times a week.
accept_en: I do exercise three times a week.
I work out three times a week.

sentences.es: Mi abuela se cuida mucho.
sentences.en: My grandmother looks after herself well.
accept_en: My grandma takes good care of herself.
My grandmother looks after herself a lot.

sentences.es: Tenía que estudiar, pero estaba muy cansado.
sentences.en: I was supposed to study, but I was very tired.
accept_en: I had to study, but I was very tired.
I needed to study, but I was really tired.
